newsitem.title: USA: U.S. blue chips firm, Nasdaq pressured by Intel.
newsitem.headline: U.S. blue chips firm, Nasdaq pressured by Intel.

text.p: U.S. blue chip stocks held to gains but were off early highs in late morning trade on Wednesday, boosted by an April Producer Price Index which pointed to benign inflation, but technology shares traded lower.

The Dow was up about 48 points, or 0.67 percent, at 7321, off a session peak of 7352. The Nasdaq composite was flat at 1333, burdened by news that Digital Equipment Corp filed a patent suit against Intel Corp.
"We're a little surprised at the strength of the Dow," said Tucker Anthony analyst Harry Laubscher. "That is a reflection of bonds, which of course are a reflection of the PPI."

The Producer Price Index slipped an unexpected 0.6 percent in April, the largest drop since August 1993, the Labor Department said. The index was expected to be flat. Excluding food and energy, the index dipped 0.1 percent.
The decline prompted analysts to say the odds of another Federal Reserve interest-rate hike next week had substantially decreased.
Treasury prices rose 25/32 points to a yield of 6.86 percent, compared with Tuesday's close of 6.93 percent.
On Nasdaq, Intel fell 1-3/8 to 151 after Digital said it would seek a "huge" damage award related to alleged patent infringement. Other chipmakers were also under pressure.
